subject: Skyward Health launch - quota & traffic coordination
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Skyward Health launch - quota & traffic coordination

Team —

Looping you in on Skyward Health's upcoming product launch (customer: Skyward Health, contact: Alex Chen). They shared an initial traffic spreadsheet (attached) and have asked for a temporary quota increase and a preflight test window ahead of their public rollout. High-level ask from the customer:

- Launch window: Oct 10-12 (phased rollout)
- Peak observed in spreadsheet: ~550 concurrent inference requests for ~12 minutes bursts during day-of promotional spikes
- Sustained morning peak: ~70 RPS for 2 hours
- Average tokens per request: ~380 (generation + rerank)

Customer request: 
1) Increase concurrent request entitlement from current 100 -> 700 for the Oct 10-12 window (with automated fallback afterward).
2) Enable a burst reservation / dedicated pool for day-of spikes.
3) A preflight synthetic test (they propose Oct 7, 02:00-04:00 UTC).

Asks for this thread: can Infra confirm feasibility and a recommended config? Neha, can you validate the spreadsheet numbers and provide an estimated node count & cost delta? Karthik / Marissa — are legal/procurement/commits required to enable this? Stephanie, can you own the rollout playbook (routing fallback / throttles / alerting)?

I've attached the customer traffic estimates and a short one-pager from Skyward. Customer is sensitive to downtime; they want a clear go/no-go 48 hours before Oct 10.

Thanks —

Kimberly Park
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: skyward_launch_traffic_estimates.xlsx, proposed_capacity_config.pdf
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-03T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Skyward Health launch - quota & traffic coordination

Kimberly — thanks for the heads-up and the attachments. Quick initial assessment from infra:

- We can support a short-duration bump to ~700 concurrent requests with a burst-enabled Dedicated pool, provided we reserve capacity ahead of time.
- Kernel & model profile note: this customer's model variant uses long-context (~2k) attention kernels and KV cache is moderately heavy; effective per-request GPU time is higher than a typical 512-token call.

What I need to lock an implementation plan:
1) Peak concurrency expressed as RPS over the burst window (you listed 550 concurrent for 12 minutes — can we confirm that correlates to ~450-600 RPS depending on request length?).
2) Confirmation of the test window and whether synthetic traffic will mirror token distribution in the spreadsheet.

Proposed infra steps:
- Reserve a Dedicated burst pool (we'd propose 8 A100-style instances for the short window, bursting to 12 if telemetry shows headroom).
- Pre-configure a routing policy: day-of route to Dedicated pool; on overload, fallback to lower-cost quantized variant (if customer approves).
- Enable prefix/KV caching for repeated prompt prefixes to reduce token compute.

Marcus
Head of Serving Infrastructure | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Date: 2027-10-03T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Skyward Health launch - quota & traffic coordination

Thanks — I reviewed the attached estimates and ran a quick sizing model based on the customer's token profile. Summary:

- Recommended baseline for the Oct 10-12 window: Dedicated pool sized for sustained 80 RPS (2h morning sustained), with capacity to burst to 600 concurrent requests for 15 minutes.
- Node plan: 8 x A100-equivalent nodes for baseline, pre-approved autoscale to 12 nodes for burst (this matches Marcus' suggestion).
- Token throughput: plan for 12M tokens/day during the window to have headroom (their sheet shows ~9.2M/day).
- Cost delta (back-of-envelope): ~+$18k for the 72-hour reserved window with burst nodes (will refine).

Test plan: Oct 7, 02:00-04:00 UTC synthetic run that mirrors: 60 RPS sustained for 30m, then two 12-minute bursts at 550-600 concurrent. We will run with the customer's staging key and collect latency/p99, GPU utilization, and queue lengths.

Preflight requirements (need these from Sales):
- Signed commitment for burst reservation (to justify node reservation)
- Confirmation that they approve fallback to quantized variant if we need to protect SLOs

I've uploaded a short capacity write-up to the shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1SkywardLaunchPrep

Neha Kapoor
Capacity Planner | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

Alex / Launch Ops —

Thanks for sharing the traffic sheet. Per our internal review (cc'd), we have a proposed capacity plan and a recommended preflight window (Oct 7, 02:00-04:00 UTC). To proceed we need two items from you:

1) Signed order form / short-term reservation for the Oct 10-12 window (I can drop the DocuSign by EOD).
2) Staging API key and a test dataset or a short set of canonical prompts so we can run synthetic traffic that matches real token distribution.

DocuSign link (placeholder): https://docs.redwood.com/s/rdw-docusign/RDW-3241

If you're comfortable, please approve the fallback behavior (our runtime may route to a quantized-compatible variant if Dedicated pool is saturated; we will only enable this with your sign-off).

I can coordinate the DocuSign and procurement. Kimberly — can you confirm the commercial terms and get Alex the proposal?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Karthik / Kimberly —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the proposed plan. Quick confirmations from our side:

- We approve the Oct 7, 02:00-03:00 UTC preflight (we'll run a subset of the synthetic plan for 1 hour — full 2h if all looks good).
- We'll sign the short-term reservation DocuSign today — finance has approved the up-front commitment.
- Staging key request: please provision a staging API key and send to launch_ops@skywardhealth.com. We'll also upload a small canonical prompt set to the Drive folder you shared.

One note on expected traffic: marketing expects smaller-than-advertised outreach on day 1 (~40% of the worst-case sheet numbers), but they may ramp to full numbers by day 3. We still want the burst safety net on day 1-3.

Also, please confirm rollback criteria (if p99 > 1.2s for more than 5 minutes, revert to scaled-down concurrency and open an incident).

Thanks — looking forward to the test.

Alex Chen
Director, Product Ops | Skyward Health
alex.chen@skywardhealth.com
